A presence that matches your ambition

We’ll make your expertise, personality, and the value you bring clear to the people you want to reach.

I’m in this with you

I’m keeping this small so you get my attention, candid feedback, and product and design expertise applied directly to your site.

A launch-ready website

When someone asks to see your work, you’ll have a site you’re proud to send them. Finished, ready to launch, and easy to update as your work grows.
<section class="outputs wrap section" id="outputs">
What you’ll build
<div class="output-tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Explore workshop outputs">
<div class="output-panel" role="tabpanel" id="panel-site" aria-labelledby="tab-site" tabindex="0">

Work out what belongs on each page, then design and build it around your expertise and the work you want to show.

  • Your pages: communicate your expertise, showcase your work, and give visitors a clear next step.
  • Desktop and mobile: adapt layouts, navigation, images, and content to each screen.
  • Your analytics: connect Google Analytics to see how people find your site and which pages they visit.
  • Your launch: connect your own domain and add your favicon, the small icon in browser tabs and bookmarks.

You own the code and content, with the ability to move hosts.

DESKTOP
MOBILE

Explore two sites I’ve built: My website · The Reading Room
<div class="output-panel" role="tabpanel" id="panel-brand" aria-labelledby="tab-brand" tabindex="0" hidden>

Create a visual language you love, then build the system that keeps it consistent.

  • Your visual identity: a logo or wordmark treatment, typography, color palette, and imagery direction.
  • Your components: consistent styles for buttons, links, and recurring page layouts.
  • Your AI reference: a brand book you can give your AI so future changes follow your design direction.
  • Room to evolve: learn how to update the system as your work and preferences grow.

Use your visual language across your site and future materials.
<div class="output-panel" role="tabpanel" id="panel-cms" aria-labelledby="tab-cms" tabindex="0" hidden>

Build the controls for the parts of your site you want to update yourself. Start with your everyday content, then learn how to make more of your site editable as your needs change.

  • Your content: copy, projects, case studies, and testimonials.
  • Your media library: upload, organize, and reuse images across your site.
  • Your SEO settings: page titles, descriptions, URLs, and image alt text.
  • Your share previews: choose the image, title, and description supplied when someone shares your site on LinkedIn or in a message.
  • Your site controls: choose which links, calls to action, and page sections you want to manage.

Add a case study, replace a photo, update your services, or publish a testimonial through your own content editor. Work with your AI coding agent to add features or make more of the site editable.
Ariba Jahan’s CMS. You’ll build a simpler version around your own content.
</section>

The workshop series

I’m keeping this group intentionally small so you can ask me questions directly and get feedback on your own site. I’ll demonstrate each step, then we’ll spend time building and working through your decisions together.
<div class="session-list">

01Set the foundation+

Set up your local AI workspace: project folders, reference files, and instructions the AI can use across sessions. Decide who the site serves, what they need to understand about your value, and the action you want them to take. Use that to decide which pages you need and the job of each page.

You leave with: a working project folder, site brief, page map, and content outline.

02Find your design direction+

Explore references and distinct directions in Claude Design using your own copy. Choose how to express your expertise and personality while keeping the visitor’s next step clear. You’ll learn how to judge and improve what AI builds: typography, spacing, layout, navigation, and how content adapts from desktop to mobile. We’ll work through what helps someone understand your value and know what to do next. Document your design choices in a brand book. Turn recurring design instructions into a reusable skill.

You leave with: your chosen design direction and a reusable visual reference.

03Build your homepage+

Move the design into Claude Code or Codex. Build the homepage and design its desktop and mobile layouts. Adapt navigation, image crops, section order, and interactions for each screen; test on your phone and practice giving the AI specific feedback. Extend those patterns to your remaining pages between sessions.

You leave with: a working homepage and a repeatable way to build the rest.

04Make it yours to update+

Build on a prepared CMS foundation. Choose the content fields and controls you need. Connect the editor to your copy, images, projects, testimonials, and page-level SEO settings. Practice adding a case study and checking the result before publishing.

You leave with: an editor configured for your site and a tested content update.

05Put it into the world+

Check mobile layouts, links, contact routes, and accessibility basics. Set page titles, descriptions, and social-sharing images. Connect your own Google Analytics account and verify a visit. Connect your domain, publish, and practice making another change and restoring an earlier version. Create a slash command for a repeatable task, such as checking a page before publishing.

You leave with: a live site and a way to keep it current.

06Q&A and site reviews+

Bring questions from finishing and using your site. Get direct help, see what others built, and work through remaining issues. Each participant also gets a bookable 30-minute individual session with Ariba Jahan.

Bring: your site, the change you want to make, or the thing you’re stuck on.

Homework after every working session. Apply what we covered to your own site, then bring that work into the next session for feedback and the next build step. Bring your existing copy, work samples, and images to the series; we’ll shape them as we build.
</section>

The tools

These are the tools I used to build my site. We’ll work through what each one does and how to use them together, from exploring a design to publishing a change.

Design

Claude Design

Explore visual directions and develop your brand book.

Build

Claude Code or Codex

Work with an AI coding agent on files on your computer.

Website

Next.js + React

Build the pages and components that make up your site.

Publish

GitHub + Vercel

Keep a history of changes and publish on your own domain.

Designing your AI workspace

Project context

Organize your files and write instructions so the AI can refer to your brief, voice, and design choices as you build.

Reusable skills

Package instructions for work you do repeatedly, such as writing a project page in your voice or following your brand book.

Slash commands

Create shortcuts for repeatable workflows, such as reviewing a page before publishing. Use and refine them on your own project.

Build with me.

Ariba Jahan

I’ve led product, innovation, and digital experience work at the Ad Council and Anomaly. I built my own site with AI and documented the decisions behind it.

Now we’ll apply that experience to yours. I’ll work with you on how your site communicates your value, give you direct design feedback, and guide you through directing the AI.

Join the founding cohort

This first series is being offered privately, with an intentionally small group. We’ll meet Thursdays at 1 p.m. ET, starting December 3. Each session runs 60–90 minutes, with a break over the holidays. Prework arrives before our first session so you can gather your content and get your tools ready.

Before you join

Who is this for?+

For solopreneurs and professionals who want a digital presence that reflects their expertise and ambition—whether you’re growing a business, exploring your next role, or making room for what comes next.

How is this different from other courses?+

We’re not just vibing. We’re using strategy and design judgment. We’ll build with AI while making deliberate choices about your brand, how your site communicates your value, and the experience people have using it. I’ll help you evaluate what’s working and guide what needs to change.

You’ll set up a local AI workspace and create a CMS you can keep updating as your work evolves. The group is intentionally small so you can ask me questions directly and get feedback on your own work throughout.

What do I need to get started?+

No prior experience with these tools is needed. Bring a computer and a paid Claude account, and allow time between sessions to work on your site. I’ll send prework covering the accounts, downloads, and files to gather.

We’ll set up your local AI workspace together, then work through GitHub, hosting, and connecting your domain. I’ll explain each tool and guide you through the setup. Your site will use Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS with your AI coding agent.

Tool subscriptions, your domain, and hosting are separate from the workshop fee; I’ll make those requirements and costs clear before enrollment.

What can I update afterward?+

Use your CMS to edit copy, manage your media library, add projects or case studies, manage testimonials, and update SEO settings. Connect your own Google Analytics account to understand visits to your site. For layout changes or new features, work with your AI coding agent, check the result, and publish the change.

When does it run, and what does it cost?+

The series starts Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 1 p.m. ET. Each of the six sessions runs 60–90 minutes. Prework will be sent ahead of the first session. The founding fee is $1,250, with $250 off your place once your buddy’s paid enrollment at $1,250 is confirmed. You’ll receive a discount code, or a $250 refund if you’ve already enrolled. Tool subscriptions, hosting, and your domain may carry separate costs; those requirements will be made clear before enrollment.

How will the schedule work?+

We meet Thursdays at 1 p.m. ET (10 a.m. PT / 6 p.m. UK). Each session runs 60–90 minutes.

Session dates: December 3, 10, and 17, 2026; January 7, 14, and 21, 2027. We’ll skip December 24 and 31 for the holidays. I’ll send prework before our first session.

If you miss a session, I’ll share a recording of the teaching portion and the session instructions so you can catch up.

If the timing is your only hesitation, email me. With a small group, there may be room to adjust the schedule together.

How does the buddy offer work?+

Your buddy enrolls at the $1,250 founding fee. Email Ariba Jahan at ariba@aribajahan.com with both of your names and enrollment email addresses so I can confirm their paid enrollment. I’ll then send you a single-use $250 discount code. If you’ve already enrolled, I’ll refund $250 to your original payment method. The discount applies to your workshop fee; the optional VIP review remains $350.

Will I own my website?+

Yes. You own the code and content, and your domain and hosting accounts are yours. Once your new site is live and your domain is connected, you can finally cancel that Squarespace website subscription. You’ll still need a domain and hosting for your new site.

Let’s build something you’re proud to put your name on.

You’ve put a lot into your work. Let’s give it a home you’re proud to share.

Wondering whether this is right for you? Email me and tell me what you have in mind.
